# Plan: SPE Round 1 (r01) for the ticket triage agent

## Summary

This is round 1. Nothing exists yet. The repo has no `spe/` folder. This round builds three things. It builds a small labeled ticket set, a first triage agent, and a code grader. Then one Workflow run measures 3 agent configurations against a no-model baseline. Your prompt is the spec. The prediction table below is the prediction. I commit locally after each step. I do not push.

## 0. Before any writes

- I confirm the working directory, the git remote, and the current branch.
- If the branch is `main`, I create `spe/r01` and work there.
- Commit messages carry no attribution lines.

## 1. Specify

### Source transcript

I save your prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`:

> "I am putting you into PLAN MODE. Let's use the SPE loop to build and evaluate the triage agent. The spec is this prompt: triage tickets correctly and cheaply. Your plan will be the first prediction, and the evals will be the dynamic workflow you run after I approve."

### Requirement table (r01)

Your prompt says "correctly" and "cheaply". It does not define either word. It does not name a ticket source or a label set. I filled those gaps with defaults. Each default is marked "Decision (default)" and logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. You can overturn any of them at approval.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns each ticket one category from a fixed list of 6: `billing`, `bug`, `access`, `outage`, `how_to`, `feature_request`. | User: "triage tickets". Decision (default) on the list. | The code grader checks that the category is in the list. |
| R2 | The agent assigns each ticket one priority: P1, P2, P3, or P4. | User: "triage tickets". Decision (default). | The code grader checks that the priority is in the set. |
| R3 | The agent returns JSON with `category`, `priority`, and a `reason` of 25 words or fewer. | Decision (default) | The code grader validates the JSON against a schema. |
| R4 | "Correctly" means category accuracy of at least 0.90 against gold labels. | User: "correctly". Decision (default) on the threshold. | Exact match against `gold.jsonl` over the eval set. |
| R5 | "Correctly" also means P1 recall of at least 0.95. Missing an urgent ticket costs more than mislabeling a minor one. | User: "correctly". Decision (default). | The grader counts the gold P1 tickets that got P1 and divides by all gold P1 tickets. |
| R6 | "Cheaply" means model cost under $5.00 per 1,000 tickets. | User: "cheaply". Decision (default). | The grader multiplies API usage tokens by a price table frozen in the harness. |
| R7 | The agent gives the same labels on repeat runs of the same ticket at least 90% of the time. | Decision (default) | The grader runs 3 repeats per ticket and computes the share with identical labels. |
| R8 | The agent sees only the ticket text and its own prompt. It never sees gold labels, graders, or predictions. | SPE method | A transcript scan voids any trial that peeked. |

### Open decisions (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default if you approve as-is |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Where real tickets come from (Jira, Zendesk, email, other) | You | Round 1 uses a synthetic set. Real tickets come in a later round. |
| D2 | The category list and the priority definitions | You | The 6 categories and 4 priorities in R1 and R2 |
| D3 | The thresholds for "correctly" and "cheaply" | You | R4, R5, and R6 |
| D4 | Who writes the gold labels | You | I write each label first and then write a ticket to fit it. I show you 15 tickets for a spot check before launch. You can waive the check. |
| D5 | The language for the agent runner | Me | Node, to match the Workflow harness |
| D6 | Which model tiers to test | You | A mid tier for C0 and C1 and a small tier for C2. I confirm current model IDs and prices from the Claude API docs before I build. |

Known threat: the same model family writes the gold labels and runs the agent. That likely inflates accuracy. To reduce this effect, I write 15 of the 100 eval tickets to be ambiguous on purpose. Each of those tickets gets a written reason for its gold label. Round 2 should add tickets labeled by a human.

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each configuration changes one thing from C0.

| Config | Description | Change from C0 |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | No model. The agent always returns the most common category and the most common priority in the eval set. This is the naive floor. | Not an agent |
| C0 | Mid-tier model, zero-shot, with category and priority definitions in the prompt, and JSON forced through a tool schema | Baseline |
| C1 | C0 plus 8 few-shot examples from a separate 20-ticket pool. The pool never overlaps the eval set. | Adds few-shot examples |
| C2 | C0 with a small-tier model | Swaps the model tier |

### Prediction table

Round 1 has no prior round, so `same_as_last_round` is null for every row.

| Metric | B0 | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 0.22 | 0.86 | 0.90 | 0.79 | `check_category_exact` | B0 equals the share of the largest class in a near-balanced set of 6. The ambiguous 15% costs C0 most of its misses. Examples fix some of the boundary cases, such as `bug` versus `outage`. The small tier loses about 7 more points on those boundaries. |
| Priority exact accuracy | 0.40 | 0.68 | 0.74 | 0.60 | `check_priority_exact` | Priority is more subjective than category. P2 versus P3 is the main source of error. |
| P1 recall | 0.00 | 0.90 | 0.93 | 0.82 | `check_p1_recall` | Outage language is strong and easy to spot. Misses come from P1 tickets written in calm language. B0 never predicts P1. |

| Cost per 1,000 tickets (USD) | 0.00 | 3.00 | 8.00 | 0.80 | `check_cost_from_usage` | This is an estimate. C0 uses about 900 input and 60 output tokens per ticket. C1 adds about 1,800 input tokens for the examples. C2 uses the same tokens as C0 at a lower price. I recompute this row from the frozen price table before I save the YAML. |

### Predicted verdicts against the spec

| Requirement | B0 | C0 | C1 | C2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R4 category accuracy at least 0.90 | Fail | Fail | Pass (at the line) | Fail |
| R5 P1 recall at least 0.95 | Fail | Fail | Fail | Fail |
| R6 cost under $5.00 per 1,000 | Pass | Pass | Fail | Pass |
| R7 stability at least 0.90 | Pass | Pass | Pass | Fail |

My headline prediction: no configuration meets all of R4 to R7 in round 1. P1 recall is the hardest requirement. Round 2 will probably target P1 recall with a cheap change.

## 3. Evaluate

### Files this round creates

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `triage/prompt.md`, `triage/run.js`, `triage/schema.json` | The agent |
| `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` | 100 eval tickets with no labels |
| `spe/evals/data/fewshot_pool.jsonl` | 20 labeled tickets for C1 only |
| `spe/evals/gold/gold.jsonl` | Gold labels and the reasons for the ambiguous tickets |
| `spe/evals/grader/grade.js`, `spe/evals/grader/prices.json` | The code grader and the frozen price table |
| `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` | The round's Workflow script |
| `spe/evals/results/r01/` | Raw trial outputs, grades, voids, and skips |

### Harness steps and gates

1. **Build the data.** I write the taxonomy doc. I write 120 tickets from labels: 100 for eval and 20 for the few-shot pool. Gate: every ticket parses. There are no duplicates. Each category has between 14 and 20 eval tickets. Each priority has at least 12 eval tickets. Then I offer you the 15-ticket spot check from D4.
2. **Build the agent.** I write the prompt, the runner, and the schema. The runner makes one API call per ticket with no tools. It logs token usage.
3. **Build the grader.** The grader is pure code with exact match on labels. No LLM judge decides a score. The one judge in this round reviews failures only.
4. **Gate: grader selftest.** The oracle (gold labels as answers) must score 1.00 on every check. An empty answer file must fail every check. A shuffled wrong answer file must score near chance.
5. **Gate: control.** No prior round exists to regrade. B0 is the control instead. The grader must return B0's category accuracy exactly as I compute it by hand from the class counts. It must return the same value on 2 runs.
6. **Gate: dry run.** I run 3 cells: C0, C1, and C2, each on 5 tickets with 1 repeat. I check that outputs parse, that the grader reads them, and that cost logging works.
7. **Commit** `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
8. **Launch the Workflow.**

### Workflow design

- `ROUND = "r01"` is a single constant. Every path and prompt reads it. No round number is written by hand in any prompt text.
- A trial is one configuration on one ticket for one repeat. Each trial returns a schema of `{round, config, ticket_id, repeat, category, priority, reason, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, error}`.
- Code checks run first. One judge agent runs at the end and only on misclassified tickets. It sorts them into failure types.
- Isolation: trial agents get the ticket path and the runner command only. After the run, a scan checks every trial transcript for reads of `spe/evals/gold/`, `spe/evals/grader/`, or `spe/predictions/`. Any trial that peeked is voided and logged.
- Split cells: a ticket is split when its 3 repeats disagree. Split tickets get up to 2 extra repeats. The cap is 60 extra trials per configuration.
- Budget: the hard cap is $15.00 of API spend. Before each trial, the harness checks the running cost plus that trial's estimated cost. It skips any trial that would cross the cap and logs the skip.
- End steps: a failure analysis agent clusters the misses into F-numbered types. A completeness critic then checks four things. Every cell must have a number. Every void and skip must be logged. Every prediction row must have a measured value. The raw outputs must match the grade totals.

### Workflow arguments

```
ROUND: "r01"
configs: ["B0", "C0", "C1", "C2"]
eval_set: spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl
fewshot_pool: spe/evals/data/fewshot_pool.jsonl  (C1 only)
repeats: 3
split_extra_repeats: 2
split_extra_cap_per_config: 60
budget_cap_usd: 15.00
max_concurrency: 8
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- Trials: 3 model configurations times 100 tickets times 3 repeats is 900 API calls. Up to 180 split retries come on top.
- Estimated API spend is about $3.50. That figure assumes the token counts in the prediction table and list prices that I still need to confirm.
- Claude Code tokens for the Workflow orchestration, the failure analysis, and the critic are an estimate of 300,000 to 600,000 tokens.
- The $15.00 cap stops the run if the estimate is far off.

## 4. Commits

All commits are local. I do not push.

| Step | Commit message |
|---|---|
| Transcript, spec table, disagreements | `SPE r01 specify: triage spec from plan-mode prompt` |
| Plan copy and predictions, before any harness work | `SPE r01 predict: 4 configs, P1 recall predicted as the blocker` |
| Data, agent, grader, gates passed | `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)` |
| Results | `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>` |
| Close-out | `SPE r01 learn: <summary>` and tag `spe-r01` |

## 5. After approval, in this order

1. I save the transcript, `spe/spec/spec.md`, and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. I commit `SPE r01 specify`.
2. I copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. I write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds the round, the date 2026-10-21, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number above with its Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`. I commit `SPE r01 predict`. I write no harness code before this commit.
3. I run harness steps 1 to 7.
4. I launch the Workflow. It returns at launch. I wait for its completion notice.
5. I commit the results.
6. Close-out. I write `spe/prediction-log.md` with the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, a "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. It also says plainly whether the B0 naive floor or a naive guess beat any prediction. I write `spe/failures.md` with each new F-numbered failure type. I add a "Proposed for round 2" table to the spec. I write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. I create `spe/README.md`. I commit `SPE r01 learn` and tag `spe-r01`.

I never edit `r01.yaml` after a trial has run.

## 6. Halt conditions

I stop and report to you in any of these cases:

- The budget cap is reached.
- A trial transcript shows a leaked answer key.
- The grader selftest or the control fails.
- One of D1 to D4 turns out to block progress and only you can decide it.

If every configuration passes every requirement, the result says the tasks are too easy. In that case round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
